t.7.60.1: As they told tales and wished for a glorious victory, the night passed swiftly for the great-souled Śatrughna.
t.7.60.2: Then, at that time, when the clear dawn had broken, that heroic Rākṣasa went forth from his city, driven by the craving for food to devour.
t.7.60.3: Meanwhile, the valiant Śatrughna, having crossed the river Yamunā, stood at the gate of Madhupura with bow in hand.
t.7.60.4: Then, when midday had come, that rākṣasa of cruel deeds arrived, carrying a load of many thousands of living creatures.
t.7.60.6: Thousands of such armed men have been devoured by me in my wrath, O vilest of men; why then do you wait for your hour?
t.7.60.5: Then he saw Śatrughna standing at the gate, weapon in hand. Looming large, the rākṣasa said to him: "What will you do with this?"
t.7.60.8: As he spoke thus and laughed again and again, Śatrughna, endowed with valour, shed tears out of rage.
t.7.60.7: This meal of mine is still incomplete, O vilest of men; how is it, O foolish one, that you have come and entered my mouth of your own accord?
t.7.60.9: From all the limbs of that great-souled Śatrughna, overcome by wrath, rays made of fiery splendour burst forth.
t.7.60.10: And Śatrughna, greatly enraged, said to that night-wanderer: "O evil-minded one, I wish to fight a single combat with you."
t.7.60.11: I am the son of Daśaratha, brother of the wise Rāma, Śatrughna by name, a slayer of foes, and I have come desiring your death.
t.7.60.12: Let single combat be granted to me, who am eager for battle. You are the enemy of all living beings; you shall not escape from me alive.
t.7.60.13: While he was speaking thus, the rākṣasa, as if laughing, replied to that best of men: "By good fortune you have come, O fool!"
t.7.60.14: The brother of my mother's sister, the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa, was slain by Rāma for the sake of a woman, O evil-minded one, O lowest of men!
t.7.60.15: All of that, the destruction of Rāvaṇa's family, I have forgiven; and holding you in contempt, I have spared you all in particular.
t.7.60.16: For all those who have not been slain by me are held in contempt by me like a blade of grass: those who have been and those who are yet to be, and you too, O vilest of men.
t.7.60.17: Since you are eager for battle, O evil-minded one, I shall give you battle of whatever kind you desire, as soon as I have readied my weapon.
t.7.60.18: Then Śatrughna said to him: "Where will you go from me alive? An enemy who has come before one, even if weak, must not be let go by one who is self-disciplined."
t.7.60.19: For he who, with a faltering mind, gave free scope to his enemy was slain because of his dull-wittedness, just as a coward is slain.
